chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him)
regarding the words of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty: ‘(Those who devour usury)...’ He said: ‘It is the man who fulfills the need of his brother, then accepts his gift.’
ai.seo_question: What does Ali ibn Abi Talib say is the meaning of 'devourers of usury' in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) offers a nuanced juristic interpretation of 'akkaluna li's-suh'ti' (devourers of usury/forbidden wealth) by extending it beyond monetary interest to include social transactions. He identifies the act of fulfilling a need and then accepting a gift as a form of subtle 'suh't' (forbidden gain), highlighting the delicate boundary between legitimate gratitude and exploitative reciprocity in Shia ethical jurisprudence.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-16 According to the same documentation, regarding the Honorable the Exalted God’s words, ‘… of devouring anything forbidden…’
Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) said, “This refers to someone who fulfills the needs of his believing brother and later accepts his gift.”
